mainTopic: Whose child it is when there are rumors; who counts as offspring for תרומה; and, in the new פרק, why a ערל כהן may not eat תרומה
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבא's limit on רב's ruling. If a woman is rumored to have been with her ארוס, the child is his, even if she is also rumored with other men. רבא proves this from the משנה 'ילדה תאכל' and a קל וחומר, but אביי answers that the משנה is a case with no rumors at all. The גמרא then explains lines of the משנה. A slave's child is not counted as his father's offspring (שמות 21:4). The words 'וזרע אין לה' teach that even an unfit child like a ממזר counts as offspring. Even the רבנן agree that a non-Jew or slave with a Jewish woman produces a ממזר. The grandmother's saying about the 'little jug' and the 'big jug' ends פרק אלמנה. The new פרק begins with a משנה about a ערל, a טמא, a פצוע דכא and a כרות שפכה, and whether they and their households may eat תרומה. The גמרא then brings the sources that a ערל may not eat תרומה: רבי אליעזר learns it from 'תושב ושכיר' by פסח, and רבי עקיבא learns it from 'איש איש'. The גמרא tests whether 'תושב ושכיר' is מופנה, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If she is rumored with him, the child is his
steps.stepSummary: רבא's limit on רב's ruling ends here: when the woman is rumored to have been with the ארוס, the child is linked to him even if there are also rumors about other men.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if she is rumored to have been with him, then even if she is also rumored to have been with others, we say the child is his.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing רבא's statement that narrows רב's ruling. If there are rumors about the woman with the ארוס himself, the child follows him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's harsh ruling (the child is a ממזר) only applies when the rumors are only about other men. Once there is also a rumor about her and the ארוס, we treat the ארוס as the father. The other rumors do not cancel that.

keyTerms.meaning: She is rumored / suspected (of being with a man)
With him (the ארוס)
With others (literally, 'from the world')
We cast it after him: we treat him as the father

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new idea starting from zero. It is the second half of רבא's limit on רב's ruling, which began just before this text.

phrases.english: But if she is rumored to have been with him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the ארוס, the man she is engaged to.

phrases.english: even if she is also rumored to have been with others,
we cast the child after him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבא's limit on רב's ruling, which began just before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rumor with the ארוס makes the child his, even when there are also rumors about other men.

steps.title: רבא's source: the משנה 'she gave birth, she may eat'
steps.stepSummary: רבא cites a משנה that says a woman who gave birth may eat תרומה. He shows it must be talking about a woman who is also rumored with other men.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: How do I know this? Because the משנה teaches: 'She gave birth, she may eat.' What is the case? If she was rumored only with him and not with others, why would the משנה need to say she may eat? Rather, it must be a case where she was also rumored with others.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a source for his idea. He reads a משנה closely to prove it is talking about a woman with rumors about other men too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the woman eat תרומה because of her child, so the child must be treated as the כהן's. If the only rumors were about the כהן, this would be too obvious to teach. So the משנה must mean a woman rumored with others as well, and still the child follows the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do I say this? (introducing a source)
She gave birth, she may eat (תרומה)
What is the case? What are the details?
Does it need to be said? (meaning, that's obvious)
Rather, isn't it...? (pushing toward the only option left)

phrases.english: Rava said: From where do I say this?
For it teaches: She gave birth, she may eat.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about a כהן who was with a בת ישראל outside of marriage. Because of the child, she may eat תרומה.

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say she is rumored to have been with him
and not rumored to have been with others,
does it need to be said that she may eat?!
Rather, is it not where she is rumored with others as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the rule in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That a rumor with the man makes the child his, even with rumors about others
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה 'ילדה תאכל', read as a case with rumors about others too

steps.title: The קל וחומר: all the more so for an ארוס
steps.stepSummary: רבא argues: if in the משנה's case the child follows the כהן, even though being with either man was forbidden, then with an ארוס, where being with him is permitted, the child should follow him all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, being with this man is forbidden and being with that man is forbidden, and still we say the child is his. Here, being with that man is forbidden but being with this man is permitted. Isn't it all the more so?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his proof with a קל וחומר, moving from the משנה's case to the ארוס case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, both men were forbidden to her, so there is no reason to favor the כהן, yet the child is his. With an ארוס, he is permitted to her by Torah law while the others are forbidden. So it is even more reasonable to assume the child is his.

keyTerms.meaning: And if there... (the opening of a קל וחומר)
Something forbidden
Something permitted
Isn't it all the more so?

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: when she is rumored with the ארוס, the child is his even with other rumors. His proof is the משנה 'ילדה תאכל' plus a קל וחומר.

phrases.english: And if there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the משנה's case of a כהן who is not married to her.

phrases.english: where being with this one is forbidden and being with that one is forbidden,
we cast the child after him,
here, where being with that one is forbidden and being with this one is permitted,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the ארוס. By Torah law she is permitted to him.

phrases.english: is it not all the more so?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה הָתָם, דִּלְהַאי אִיסּוּרָא וּלְהַאי אִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the reading of the משנה from step 2 and applies it to the ארוס case.
steps.raayaObject: The rule in step 1 about an ארוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the משנה's case (both men forbidden) to the ארוס case (he is permitted)

steps.title: אביי: רב says ממזר whenever there are rumors with others
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's reading. He says רב calls the child a ממזר whenever she is rumored with others, even if also with the ארוס, and the משנה is a case with no rumors at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Really, I can tell you that anywhere she is rumored with others, even if she is also rumored with him, רב said the child is a ממזר. And the משנה is talking about a case where she is not rumored with anyone at all.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבא's limit and on his proof. He reads the משנה in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's proof depended on the משנה being a case with rumors about others, since otherwise it seemed too obvious. אביי says the משנה is a case with no rumors at all, so it proves nothing about rumors with others. Because of that, רב's ruling of ממזר applies whenever there are rumors about other men.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, I can tell you (keeping the original position)
The child is a ממזר
Where she is not rumored at all

steps.whatToRemember: רבא and אביי disagree about how far רב's ממזר ruling reaches. For אביי, any rumor with other men makes the child a ממזר, and the משנה is a case with no rumors.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not rejecting the משנה. He only says it is talking about a different case (no rumors at all), so it cannot prove רבא's point.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
phrases.english: Abaye said to him: Actually, I can say to you
anywhere that she is rumored to have been with others,
even if she is also rumored to have been with him,
Rav said: The child is a mamzer.
And the Mishnah is where she is not rumored at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's proof (steps 2-3) and the limit he put on רב's ruling (step 1).
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Both רבא's limit on רב's ruling and his proof from the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as a case with no rumors at all, so it does not show that the child follows the man when there are rumors about others.

steps.title: Why a slave does not disqualify as offspring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that an עבד disqualifies only through ביאה, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a slave disqualifies a woman from eating תרומה through relations, but not as her offspring. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a descendant of a כהן's daughter from a non-כהן keeps her from going back to eat תרומה. The משנה says an עבד descendant does not have this power. The גמרא wants to know why he is not counted as her offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish slave
Disqualifies, here from eating תרומה
Relations, intimacy
What is the reason?

phrases.english: A slave disqualifies because of relations, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. The 'etc.' stands for the rest of the line: but he does not disqualify as her offspring.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב/רבא/אביי discussion and opens a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for why an עבד is not counted as a woman's offspring for תרומה.

steps.title: A slave woman's children are hers alone
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק saying a שפחה's children belong to the master, so they are not counted as the father's family.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'The wife and her children shall be her master's.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק about a שפחה married to an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the שפחה's children stay with her master. That shows they follow only their mother and have no family link to their father. So such a child is not counted as offspring of his father's side, and he cannot disqualify his grandmother.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says
And her children
Etc., the rest of the פסוק (written וגו׳)

phrases.english: The verse says:
"The wife and her children shall be, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:4. The פסוק ends 'to her master.' The children are hers, not their father's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שפחה's children are counted as hers alone, so they are not offspring of their father's family.
steps.whatToRemember: A child born to a שפחה follows only his mother. He is not counted as family on his father's side, so he does not disqualify his father's mother from תרומה.

steps.title: A grandchild also counts as offspring
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's ממזר line, a ברייתא learns from 'וזרע אין לה' that even a grandchild counts as her offspring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a ממזר disqualifies and also lets a woman eat. The רבנן taught: 'And she has no offspring.' This would only teach about her own child. How do we know her grandchild counts too? The פסוק says 'offspring' to include any kind.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ממזר line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that reads the פסוק about a כהן's daughter returning to her father's house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah lets a כהן's daughter who is widowed or divorced eat תרומה again only if she has no offspring. The ברייתא says the word זרע includes descendants of any kind, so a grandchild also stops her. This is the first of two teachings from the same phrase.

keyTerms.meaning: A child of a forbidden union (like adultery)
Lets someone eat (תרומה)
The Rabbis taught; introduces a ברייתא
Offspring, descendants
The פסוק teaches
In any case, of any kind

phrases.english: A mamzer disqualifies and lets her eat.
phrases.notes: Another quote from the משנה. A ממזר counts as offspring, so sometimes he stops her from eating and sometimes he lets her eat.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And she has no offspring":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:13

phrases.english: I would only know about her own child;
from where do we know about her child's child?
The verse teaches: "And she has no offspring"
of any kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה (ממזר) and brings a ברייתא on what counts as זרע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A grandchild counts as offspring and keeps a כהן's daughter from going back to eat תרומה.

steps.title: An unfit child also counts as offspring
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: from the same phrase, read as 'עיין עליה', even an unfit child like a ממזר counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: This would only teach about a fit child. How do we know an unfit child counts too? The פסוק says 'And she has no offspring.' Read it as: check her out.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second teaching from the same words, and this is the source for the משנה's ממזר rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words אין לה ('she has none') are read with a wordplay as עיין עליה ('examine her'). That means: check for any offspring at all, fit or unfit. So a ממזר also counts as her offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: A fit, valid child
An unfit child, like a ממזר
Examine her, check her out (wordplay on אין לה)

phrases.english: I would only know about a fit child;
from where do we know about an unfit child?
The verse teaches: "And she has no offspring":
examine her.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: אֵין לָהּ sounds like עַיֵּין עָלֶיהָ. Check whether she has any child at all, fit or not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second teaching of the same ברייתא from the same phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An unfit child, like a ממזר, counts as offspring for תרומה.
steps.confusionAlert: The same words 'וזרע אין לה' are used twice in a row. Step 7 used them for grandchildren, and this step uses them for an unfit child. That double use is exactly what the next step questions.

steps.title: The phrase was already used for grandchildren
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the phrase was already used to teach about grandchildren, so how can it also teach about an unfit child?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already used this phrase for her grandchild!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for using one phrase to teach two separate things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one phrase in a פסוק is used for one teaching. The ברייתא learned grandchildren from 'וזרע אין לה' and then used the same words again for an unfit child. The גמרא asks where the extra source comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely; opens a challenge
You already used it (for something else)

phrases.english: But you already used it for her child's child!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא's double use of the same phrase in steps 7 and 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of 'וזרע אין לה' for both grandchildren and an unfit child.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One phrase cannot be the source for two separate teachings.

steps.title: Grandchildren need no verse, so it teaches about an unfit child
steps.stepSummary: The phrase was never really needed for grandchildren, since grandchildren are like children anyway. It is needed only for an unfit child.
steps.simpleTranslation: For her grandchild no פסוק was needed, because grandchildren are like children. The פסוק was needed for an unfit child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the phrase really teaches only one thing, the unfit child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a general rule that בני בנים are like בנים, so a grandchild counts even without a פסוק. The ברייתא mentioned it only by the way. The phrase's real job is to include an unfit child like a ממזר, which supports the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: No פסוק was needed
Grandchildren are treated like children

phrases.english: For her child's child, no verse was needed,
since grandchildren are like children.
Where the verse was needed
was for an unfit child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removing one of the two teachings from the פסוק because it is already known from a general rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The phrase was needed for both grandchildren and an unfit child.
steps.terutzMaskana: Grandchildren are known from the rule that grandchildren are like children. The phrase teaches only about an unfit child.
steps.whatToRemember: Grandchildren count as offspring because בני בנים הרי הן כבנים. The פסוק 'וזרע אין לה' is what teaches that even an unfit child like a ממזר counts. That is the source for the משנה's rule that a ממזר disqualifies and lets her eat.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the משנה's ruling that a ממזר counts as offspring for תרומה, both to disqualify and to let her eat.

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks whose view the משנה follows
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks רבי יוחנן whether the משנה, which treats the child of a Jewish woman and a non-Jew or slave as a ממזר, follows only רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to רבי יוחנן: Whose opinion is this? Is it only like רבי עקיבא, who holds that a ממזר can come even from a relationship forbidden by a regular לאו?
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש is asking which תנא the משנה agrees with when it treats such a child as a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that a ממזר comes even from a relationship that is only a לאו. The רבנן hold that a ממזר comes only from a relationship punished by כרת. So ריש לקיש worries the משנה matches only רבי עקיבא's minority view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? (Whose opinion is this?)
Relationships forbidden by a regular negative commandment (a לאו)
A child born from a forbidden relationship, who may not marry an ordinary Jew

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said to Rabbi Yochanan:
According to whom? Is it like Rabbi Akiva,
who said: a mamzer can come even from those who violate a regular prohibition?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גמרא showed that an unfit child like a ממזר counts as offspring, ריש לקיש asks which view the משנה's ממזר case assumes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the משנה's assumption that the child of a non-Jew or slave and a Jewish woman is a ממזר follow only רבי עקיבא?

steps.title: Even the Rabbis agree about a non-Jew and a slave
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה can follow the רבנן too, because they agree that a non-Jew or slave with a Jewish woman produces a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows the רבנן. In the case of a non-Jew or a slave, they agree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers ריש לקיש: the משנה does not have to follow only רבי עקיבא, since the רבנן agree in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן usually require כרת to make a ממזר. But for a non-Jew or slave they agree the child is a ממזר anyway. So the משנה fits everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (it fits even this other view)
The Sages, the majority opinion
They agree

phrases.english: You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
since in the case of a non-Jew and a slave, they agree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה can follow the רבנן too, because they agree that the child of a non-Jew or slave and a Jewish woman is a ממזר.

steps.title: Proof from רבי's teaching brought by רב דימי
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that רבי taught that a non-Jew or slave with a Jewish woman produces a ממזר, which shows the רבנן agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said that רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said in the name of our teacher: If a non-Jew or a slave has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the last answer with a teaching that רב דימי brought from ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) rules plainly that such a child is a ממזר, with no כרת needed. This supports the claim that even the רבנן accept a ממזר in this case, so the משנה is not just רבי עקיבא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל with teachings)
Our teacher, meaning רבי יהודה הנשיא
The child

steps.whatToRemember: The child of a non-Jew or slave and a Jewish woman is a ממזר according to everyone, not only רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: For when Rav Dimi came,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר אַבְדִּימִי מִשּׁוּם רַבֵּינוּ:
phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi said in the name of our teacher:
phrases.notes: "Our teacher" here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: A non-Jew or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman:
the child is a mamzer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source that supports the answer in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן agree a non-Jew or slave with a Jewish woman produces a ממזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב דימי's report of רבי יצחק בר אבדימי in the name of רבי: the child is a ממזר.

steps.title: The grandmother's saying about her two grandsons
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's line that a כהן גדול can disqualify his grandmother from תרומה, a ברייתא quotes her: she treasures the ממזר grandson who lets her eat תרומה, not the כהן גדול grandson who stops her.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said a כהן גדול sometimes disqualifies. The רבנן taught that the grandmother says: I would gladly be an atonement for my daughter's son, the little jug, since he lets me eat תרומה. But I am not an atonement for my daughter's son, the big jug, since he disqualifies me from תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא with the grandmother's colorful saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The "little jug" is the ממזר grandson, unimportant in status, who keeps her eating תרומה. The "big jug" is the important כהן גדול grandson, who stops her from eating it. The irony shows that what matters for תרומה is family line, not the grandson's honor.

keyTerms.meaning: The High Priest
The Rabbis taught (introduces a ברייתא)
An atonement for (an expression of love: "let me suffer in his place")
A small jug / a large jug
The holy portion of produce given to כהנים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the jugs: the "little jug" is the ממזר, who helps her eat תרומה. The "big jug" is the כהן גדול, who stops her.

phrases.english: A High Priest sometimes disqualifies.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: a כהן גדול grandson can sometimes stop his grandmother from eating תרומה.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
I am hereby an atonement for my daughter's son, the little jug,
phrases.notes: The "little jug" is the ממזר grandson. She is saying he is dear to her.

phrases.english: since he lets me eat terumah;
but I am not an atonement for my daughter's son, the big jug,
since he disqualifies me from terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, פְּעָמִים שֶׁפּוֹסֵל. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה about the כהן גדול grandson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ממזר grandson can let his grandmother keep eating תרומה, while a כהן גדול grandson can disqualify her. This is expressed through her saying about the little and big jugs.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אלמנה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק אלמנה לכהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אלמנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The פרק ends here with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן means "we will return to you," a promise to come back and learn this פרק again. It is not part of the argument. It only marks the end of the chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
The name of the פרק just finished (אלמנה לכהן גדול)

phrases.english: We will return to you, Almanah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק that the previous steps belonged to.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק אלמנה לכהן גדול is complete.

steps.title: New פרק: a ערל or טמא כהן may not eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens: a ערל כהן and any טמא כהן may not eat תרומה, but their wives and slaves may.
steps.simpleTranslation: An uncircumcised כהן and all who are טמא may not eat תרומה. Their wives and their slaves may eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה about who may and may not eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem of being a ערל or טמא is personal to the כהן himself. It does not take away his status as a כהן. So the wives and slaves he acquired through that status may still eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncircumcised man (here, a כהן who was not circumcised)
Those who are ritually impure
Their wives and their slaves

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the theme of the new פרק: some problems block only the כהן himself, while others also affect his household.

phrases.english: An uncircumcised man and all who are ritually impure
may not eat terumah.
Their wives and their slaves may eat terumah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶעָרֵל וְכׇל הַטְּמֵאִים לֹא יֹאכְלוּ בִּתְרוּמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערל or טמא כהן may not eat תרומה, but his wives and slaves may.

steps.title: An injured כהן eats תרומה, but his wife may not
steps.stepSummary: A כהן who is a פצוע דכא or כרות שפכה keeps eating תרומה, and so do his slaves. His wife may not eat, unless he has not been with her since the injury.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man with crushed testicles or a severed member: he and his slaves may eat תרומה, but his wife may not. If he has not been with her since the injury, the wives may eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of כהנים with problems. This time the rule flips: the man eats, but his wife does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the ערל and the טמא in the previous step, this כהן is still fully a כהן, so he and his slaves eat. The problem is his marriage. Such a man may not live with a Jewish woman, so once he is with her after the injury, she loses her right to תרומה. If he has not been with her since then, she keeps it.

keyTerms.meaning: A man whose testicles are crushed or wounded
A man whose member has been cut off
He was intimate with her (literally, he 'knew' her)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the previous step. There, the ערל and טמא could not eat but their wives could. Here it is the opposite: the man eats and his wife cannot.

phrases.english: A man with crushed testicles or one with a severed member:
they and their slaves may eat [תרומה],
but their wives may not eat.
And if he did not have relations with her
since he became one with crushed testicles or a severed member,
these [wives] may eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּצוּעַ דַּכָּא וּכְרוּת שׇׁפְכָה הֵן וְעַבְדֵיהֶן יֹאכֵלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of כהנים whose condition affects who in their household eats תרומה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The injured כהן and his slaves eat תרומה. His wife does not, unless he has not been with her since the injury.

steps.title: Defining פצוע דכא and כרות שפכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines both terms. A wound to even one testicle makes a פצוע דכא. A כרות שפכה is one whose member was cut off, but if even a hair's width of the corona remains, he is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is a פצוע דכא? Anyone whose testicles were wounded, even one of them. A כרות שפכה is anyone whose member was cut off. But if even a hair's width of the corona is left, he is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains exactly what counts as each of the two injuries it just mentioned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a פצוע דכא, the standard is strict: an injury to just one testicle is enough. For a כרות שפכה, the line is the corona. As long as even a tiny bit of it remains, he is still fit and keeps his normal status.

keyTerms.meaning: The corona (the rim at the head of the member)
As thin as a hair, the smallest possible amount
Fit, meaning he keeps his normal status

steps.whatToRemember: One wounded testicle is enough to make a פצוע דכא. A כרות שפכה stays fit as long as any bit of the corona remains.

phrases.english: And who is a man with crushed testicles?
Anyone whose testicles were wounded,
even just one of them.
And one with a severed member
is anyone whose member was cut off.
But if some of the corona remained,
even as thin as a hair,
he is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the two terms used in the previous ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wound to even one testicle makes a פצוע דכא. A כרות שפכה with any bit of corona left is fit.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a ערל may not eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא in which רבי אלעזר asks for the source that a ערל may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא teaches that רבי אלעזר asked: From where do we know that a ערל may not eat תרומה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה's first rule, that a ערל כהן may not eat תרומה. This line sets up the question, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated this rule without giving a source. The ברייתא asks where in the Torah it comes from, since no פסוק in the תרומה section openly says it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
From where do we know? A request for a Torah source
An uncircumcised man

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Elazar said:
From where do we know that an uncircumcised man
may not eat תרומה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by returning to the ערל rule stated in the opening of the new משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source that a ערל may not eat תרומה

steps.title: רבי אלעזר learns it from קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: The same words "תושב ושכיר" appear for both קרבן פסח and תרומה. Since a ערל may not eat the פסח, he may not eat תרומה either.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words "a sojourner and a hired servant" appear about the פסח, and they also appear about תרומה. Just as with the פסח a ערל is forbidden, so too with תרומה a ערל is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers his own question with a גזירה שווה, linking תרומה to the פסח through a shared phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah openly forbids a ערל from eating the פסח. Because the same words "תושב ושכיר" appear in both sections, the rule of the פסח carries over to תרומה. So a ערל may not eat תרומה either.

keyTerms.meaning: A sojourner and a hired servant, the shared words that link the two topics
Learning a law from one topic to another because the Torah uses the same words in both
The קרבן פסח, the Passover offering

phrases.english: It says "a sojourner and a hired servant" about the פסח,
phrases.notes: שמות 12:45

phrases.english: and it says "a sojourner and a hired servant" about תרומה.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10

phrases.english: Just as with "a sojourner and a hired servant" said about the פסח,
an uncircumcised man is forbidden to eat it,
so too with "a sojourner and a hired servant" said about תרומה,
an uncircumcised man is forbidden to eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of the previous step
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שווה from the words "תושב ושכיר" carries the פסח's ban on a ערל over to תרומה

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns it from "איש איש"
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says the גזירה שווה is unnecessary. The doubled word "איש איש" in the פסוק about טמאים already includes the ערל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: That is not needed, because the פסוק says "איש איש" (any man), which comes to include the ערל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא offers a different, simpler source for the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two do not disagree about the law: both hold that a ערל may not eat תרומה. They disagree only about the source. רבי עקיבא reads the extra word "איש" in the פסוק about a טמא כהן as adding the ערל to that list, so he needs no comparison to the פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed; that proof is unnecessary
"A man, a man" (any man), a doubled word read as adding something
To include, to add to the rule

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that a ערל may not eat תרומה. רבי אלעזר learns it from the פסח through "תושב ושכיר", and רבי עקיבא learns it from the doubled "איש איש".

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says: This is not needed,
for the verse says "any man" (literally, "a man, a man"),
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:4. This פסוק is about a כהן who is טמא and may not eat holy food.

phrases.english: to include the uncircumcised man.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule and says the previous derivation is unneeded
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubled "איש איש" includes the ערל among those who may not eat holy food, so no גזירה שווה is needed.

steps.title: The גמרא re-quotes רבי אליעזר's comparison so it can examine it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבי אליעזר's גזירה שווה from the ברייתא: "תושב ושכיר" appears by פסח and by תרומה, so just as a ערל may not eat the פסח, he may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי אליעזר says: "תושב ושכיר" is said about the פסח, and "תושב ושכיר" is said about תרומה. Just as with the פסח a ערל is forbidden, so too with תרומה a ערל is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the ברייתא again so it can now study it closely. This step sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. The words "אמר מר" tell us the גמרא is returning to an earlier quote to ask about how the proof works. The next steps will check whether this גזירה שווה really holds.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Master said". The גמרא is quoting an earlier source again in order to discuss it
"A resident and a hired worker". These words appear both by פסח and by תרומה
The קרבן פסח, the Passover offering

phrases.english: The Master said:
Rabbi Eliezer says:
"A resident and a hired worker" is said about the Pesach,
phrases.notes: שמות 12:45

phrases.english: and "a resident and a hired worker" is said about teruma.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:10

phrases.english: Just as with "a resident and a hired worker" said about the Pesach,
an uncircumcised man is forbidden in it,
so too with "a resident and a hired worker" said about teruma,
an uncircumcised man is forbidden in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבי אליעזר's גזירה שווה from step 20 in order to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערל may not eat תרומה, learned from פסח through the shared words "תושב ושכיר".

steps.title: The words must be free, or the comparison could be broken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the גזירה שווה only works if the words are מופנה. Otherwise one could argue that the פסח is special because it carries פיגול, נותר and טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It must be free. For if it is not free, there is a way to refute it: what about the פסח? It is special because one is liable for it on account of פיגול, נותר and טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets a condition for the proof. The repeated words must be extra, because otherwise a difference between פסח and תרומה would break the comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזירה שווה can be knocked down by showing the source is stricter than the target. The פסח is a קרבן with serious כרת-level rules like פיגול, נותר and eating while טמא. So maybe only something that holy is forbidden to a ערל, and תרומה would not be.

keyTerms.meaning: "Free" or "available". The words are not needed for their own context, so they can be used for a גזירה שווה
"One can refute it", meaning there is a logical difference that breaks the comparison
A קרבן brought with the wrong intention about when it would be eaten
Meat of a קרבן left over past its time
Ritually impure. Here it means eating a קרבן while impure

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the גזירה שווה fails. It is saying the גזירה שווה needs free words to survive this kind of attack, and the next step says the words are free.

phrases.english: It must be free.
phrases.notes: The words "תושב ושכיר" have to be extra in their own פסוק before we can learn from them this way.

phrases.english: For if it is not free,
there is a way to refute it:
What about the Pesach?
It is special, since one is liable for it
on account of piggul, notar, and impurity.

steps.triggerLanguage: מוּפְנֶה. דְּאִי לָאו מוּפְנֶה אִיכָּא לְמִיפְרַךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a condition for the גזירה שווה quoted in step 22 by pointing to a possible refutation.
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שווה from פסח to תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסח has stricter rules (פיגול, נותר, טמא), so a law about it might not carry over to the less severe תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גזירה שווה requires the words to be מופנה.

steps.title: The words really are free
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the refutation does not apply, because the words are in fact free.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not so. It is indeed free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the attack from the last step does not work, because the words are free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the words of a גזירה שווה are extra, a logical difference between the two cases cannot break it. So the stricter rules of the פסח do not matter here. This claim, though, raises the question of which פסוק has the free words.

keyTerms.meaning: "Not so". It rejects the possible objection
"It is indeed free". The words truly are extra

phrases.english: Not so,
it is indeed free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the possible refutation from step 23 by saying the words are free.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The words are declared free, so the logical refutation does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The stricter nature of the פסח could break the comparison.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the words are free, the גזירה שווה holds despite the differences.

steps.title: Which of the two phrases is the free one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which appearance of "תושב ושכיר" is extra: the one by תרומה or the one by פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is free?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question to check the claim it just made. This sets up a test of each פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying the words are free is not enough. One of the two פסוקים has to be shown to have words it does not need for its own law. The גמרא now checks each one.

keyTerms.meaning: "Which?"

phrases.english: Which one is free?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of the claim in step 24 that the words are free.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק, the תרומה one or the פסח one, has the extra "תושב ושכיר".

steps.title: The words by תרומה are needed for their own law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the words cannot be the free ones in the תרומה פסוק, because they are needed there.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the one by תרומה, those words are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option, the תרומה פסוק, and rejects it. Those words already teach something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Words that teach their own law are not extra, so they cannot be the free side of the גזירה שווה. The proof for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: "They are certainly needed". The words have their own job

phrases.english: If it is the one about teruma,
those words are certainly needed,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to step 25 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the תרומה פסוק is the free one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Those words teach their own law, so they are not extra.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows what תושב and שכיר teach about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that תושב is a Jewish slave acquired until the יובל, and שכיר is one acquired for six years. This shows the words have a job by תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: "תושב" is one acquired with a permanent acquisition, and "שכיר" is one acquired with an acquisition of years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the תרומה words are needed. Each word refers to a different kind of slave who may not eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives each word its own meaning: two types of Jewish slaves of a כהן who may not eat תרומה. Since both words are used up, they are not free for the גזירה שווה.

keyTerms.meaning: "As it is taught in a ברייתא"
Acquired permanently, meaning until the יובל
Acquired for a set number of years (six)

phrases.english: as it is taught:
"Resident": this is one acquired with a permanent acquisition,
phrases.notes: This is a Jewish slave whose ear was pierced, so he stays with his master until the יובל.

phrases.english: "Hired worker": this is one acquired with an acquisition of years.
phrases.notes: He means the regular six-year Jewish slave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 26's claim that the תרומה words are needed.
steps.raayaObject: That "תושב ושכיר" by תרומה is not extra
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading the words as two kinds of Jewish slaves

steps.title: The ברייתא asks why both words are needed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: why not write only תושב? If a permanent slave may not eat תרומה, a six-year slave surely may not, by a קל וחומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it say "תושב" and not say "שכיר", and I would say: if one acquired permanently does not eat, then one acquired for years, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the ברייתא, a question is raised: the word שכיר seems extra, because a קל וחומר from תושב would already teach it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A permanent slave is more fully tied to the כהן's household than a six-year slave. So if even he cannot eat תרומה, the six-year slave surely cannot. This challenges whether שכיר has its own job. The next step gives the ברייתא's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: "Let it say". It suggests the פסוק could have written less
"All the more so". This is the wording of a קל וחומר
Reasoning from a stronger case to a weaker one

steps.confusionAlert: This question belongs to the ברייתא itself, not to the גמרא's main discussion. If it succeeded, the word שכיר by תרומה would be extra.

phrases.english: But let it say "resident"
and not say "hired worker",
and I would say:
if one acquired with a permanent acquisition does not eat,

phrases.aramaic: קָנוּי קִנְיַן שָׁנִים לֹא כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן!
phrases.english: then one acquired for years, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in step 27 by suggesting the word שכיר could be learned through a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the word שכיר in the תרומה פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from the permanent slave would already forbid the six-year slave, so שכיר seems extra.

steps.title: Why both words are needed by תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers its own question. With only one word, we would have thought a permanent slave may eat תרומה, so ״שכיר״ is written to teach that he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If only one word were written, I would have read it as the six-year slave and said the permanent slave may eat. ״שכיר״ comes to teach about ״תושב״ that even a permanent slave may not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the קל וחומר question from step 28. It shows that both words really are needed in the תרומה פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed the permanent slave is the 'stronger' case for not eating. The ברייתא says you could just as easily think the opposite: a permanent slave is more fully his master's, so maybe he does eat. Writing both words blocks that mistake, so the תרומה words are not free.

keyTerms.meaning: a permanent acquisition (the slave who stays until the יוֹבֵל)
an acquisition for a set number of years (six years)
it comes and teaches (one word explains the other)
he may eat (here: eat תְּרוּמָה)

phrases.english: Had it been so, I would have said:
phrases.notes: He means: had the Torah written only one of the two words.

phrases.english: 'תושב' — this is one acquired for years,
but one acquired permanently may eat,
so 'שכיר' came and taught about 'תושב',

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁקָּנוּי קִנְיַן עוֹלָם — אֵין אוֹכֵל.
phrases.english: that even though he is acquired permanently, he may not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's question from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the opposite reasoning was possible, so the קל וחומר could not be relied on.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Write only one word; the other follows by קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both words are needed by תרומה, so neither is free there.

steps.title: So the פסח words must be the free ones
steps.stepSummary: Since the תרומה words are needed, the גמרא concludes that the ״תושב ושכיר״ written by פסח are the free ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the words by פסח are free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from step 25: the free words are the ones by פסח. This also sets up the next question about what those words mean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 offered two options, תרומה or פסח. Steps 26 to 29 ruled out תרומה, so by elimination the גמרא points to פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: free, extra words that are available for a גְּזֵירָה שָׁוָה
rather (turning to the other option)

phrases.english: Rather, those of the Paschal lamb are free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תרומה option is ruled out, the גמרא turns to the פסח option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The free ״תושב ושכיר״ is the one written by פסח.

steps.title: What does ״תושב ושכיר״ by פסח mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the ״תושב ושכיר״ in the פסח פסוק refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: This ״תושב ושכיר״ that the Torah wrote by פסח: what is it talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the words in the פסח פסוק actually mean. This sets up the next move, which checks whether the words could have a job of their own there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To call the פסח words free, the גמרא must show they teach nothing in their own place. So it first asks what they would mean if read plainly.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks the claim from step 30 by asking what the פסח words mean.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is meant by ״תושב ושכיר״ in the פסח פסוק?

steps.title: A real Hebrew slave has no reason to be exempt from פסח
steps.stepSummary: If the words mean an actual Hebrew slave, it makes no sense that being a slave would exempt him from פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means a real תושב and שכיר, would he be exempt from פסח just because he is a תושב or שכיר?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the plain reading, that the words mean a real Hebrew slave. It finds that reading hard to accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Hebrew slave is a full Jew, and his slave status should not take him out of the מצוה of פסח. So reading the פסח words as a real slave leads to a strange law.

keyTerms.meaning: actual, literal
he is exempt
if we say

phrases.english: If we say it means an actual sojourner and hired servant,
then because he is a sojourner or hired servant
he is exempt from the Paschal lamb?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the פסח words as an actual Hebrew slave.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being a Hebrew slave gives no reason to be exempt from the מצוה of פסח.

steps.title: Proof from תרומה that he is not his master's property
steps.stepSummary: We already know a Hebrew slave may not eat his כהן master's תרומה, which shows he is not treated as his master's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we hold regarding תרומה that he does not eat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its challenge with a known rule: a Hebrew slave does not eat his master's תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might argue that a Hebrew slave is exempt from פסח because he belongs to his master, like a כנעני slave. But the תרומה rule shows he is not counted as his master's property, so that argument fails. That leaves the plain reading of the פסח words without a sensible meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: we hold, it is established for us
regarding, in the case of
the portion of produce given to a כֹּהֵן

steps.whatToRemember: The תרומה words are needed, so the גמרא checks the פסח words. A real Hebrew slave has no reason to be exempt from פסח, since תרומה shows he is not his master's property.

phrases.english: But we hold regarding תרומה
phrases.notes: This is the rule from the ברייתא in steps 27 to 29: a Hebrew slave may not eat his כהן master's תרומה.

phrases.english: that he does not eat!
